messages.content: What is NICE guidance HTG293 about?
HTG293 is HealthTech guidance titled "Laparoscopic gastric plication for the treatment of severe obesity".
When was HTG293 published?
What type of NICE guidance is HTG293?
HealthTech guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in HTG293?

Only use with special arrangements for clinical governance, consent and audit or research. Patients should be informed of uncertainties about long-term efficacy and about how the procedure may affect the safety of any later gastric surgery. It should be performed only in bariatric surgery units able to offer it among a range of treatment options, with patient outcomes reported to the National Bariatric Surgery Registry.
What condition or clinical problem does HTG293 address?
Severe obesity, defined as BMI 40 kg/m2 or more, or BMI 35 to under 40 kg/m2 with significant comorbidities such as hypertension or diabetes.
Who is the target population in HTG293?
Adults with severe obesity for whom non-surgical weight-management measures have been insufficient and bariatric surgery is being considered.
What intervention is covered by HTG293?
Laparoscopic gastric plication
What is the current care or treatment standard described in HTG293?
Dietary advice, exercise, lifestyle change and medicines; bariatric surgery is considered for selected patients who have not lost enough weight with non-surgical measures.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does HTG293 report?

Case series reported mean excess weight loss of 65% at a mean 23-month follow-up in 135 patients, 54% at 6 months and 60% at 24 months in 100 patients. In the 135-patient series, 21% had inadequate excess weight loss (<50%) and 6% met a failure definition (<30%). Improvements in back pain, diabetes, hypertension and sleep apnoea were reported; a small 15-patient series found a significant IWQOL-Lite improvement after greater-curvature plication but not anterior plication.
What comparator or comparison does HTG293 use?
No comparative cost-effectiveness evaluation is presented; evidence consists mainly of case series.
What are the main safety considerations in HTG293?

No major short-term safety concern was identified, but long-term safety is inadequate, particularly reversibility and implications for later gastric surgery. Reported complications included portomesenteric thrombosis with jejunal necrosis, gastric perforation, obstruction from fundus herniation, suture-line leaks, liver haematoma/abscess, seroma causing obstruction, gastrointestinal bleeding, hypocalcaemia and prolonged nausea/vomiting.
What does the economic evaluation in HTG293 show?
No formal economic model or ICER is reported in this HealthTech guidance.
What does HTG293 say about budget impact or affordability?
No national budget impact estimate is reported. Feasibility depends on specialist bariatric centres, governance, audit/research arrangements and registry reporting.
What does HTG293 say about patient quality of life?
A small case series reported improved IWQOL-Lite after greater-curvature plication.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in HTG293?
Guidance highlights equality duties and requires local implementation consistent with non-discrimination; specialist bariatric-centre delivery may limit access to appropriately equipped services.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in HTG293?

- Limited short- and medium-term efficacy evidence. - Insufficient long-term efficacy evidence and durability data. - Insufficient long-term safety evidence, especially reversibility and impact on subsequent gastric surgery.
How should the recommendation in HTG293 be implemented in practice?
Inform governance leads; obtain informed consent with clear written information; use specialist bariatric units; collect and submit outcomes to the National Bariatric Surgery Registry.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about HTG293?
Procedure reduces gastric volume by plicating the stomach without removing gastric tissue and is potentially reversible. NICE requires research/audit and specialist bariatric governance.
What is NICE guidance HTG323 about?
HTG323 is HealthTech guidance titled "Implantation of a duodenal–jejunal bypass sleeve for managing obesity".
When was HTG323 published?
What type of NICE guidance is HTG323?
HealthTech guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in HTG323?

Only use DJBS implantation in the context of research. Clinicians should review local clinical outcomes and enter details of all patients on the National Bariatric Surgery Register. NICE calls for well-controlled studies documenting patient selection, complications while the device is in place and after removal, and technical problems with implantation/removal.
What condition or clinical problem does HTG323 address?
Obesity, defined as BMI 30 kg/m2 or more, associated with comorbidities including type 2 diabetes, coronary heart disease and hypertension.
Who is the target population in HTG323?
People with obesity for whom DJBS is being considered to support weight loss and potentially improve obesity-related comorbidities, including diabetes.
What intervention is covered by HTG323?
Duodenal–jejunal bypass sleeve (DJBS)
What is the current care or treatment standard described in HTG323?
Dietary advice, exercise, lifestyle change and medicines; bariatric surgery is considered in selected patients with severe obesity or obesity with significant comorbidities.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does HTG323 report?

In an RCT of 56 patients, DJBS produced 11.9% versus 2.7% excess weight loss at 12 weeks versus sham (p=0.001). A 42-patient case series reported 47.0% excess weight loss at 52 weeks. In an 18-patient obesity/type 2 diabetes RCT, HbA1c reductions were larger numerically with DJBS than sham at 12 and 24 weeks but were not statistically significant.
What comparator or comparison does HTG323 use?
Comparators included sham endoscopy in small randomised studies; clinical indications remained uncertain.
What are the main safety considerations in HTG323?

Important adverse events included gastrointestinal bleeding with haematemesis in 14% (3/21) in one RCT, device migration in 41% (5/12) in another, sleeve obstruction, mucosal tears, nausea and upper abdominal pain, pseudopolyp formation and implant-site inflammation. Specialist advisers also cited possible jejunal ulceration/perforation, duodenal wall erosion and difficulties removing obstructed/migrated devices.
What does the economic evaluation in HTG323 show?
No formal economic model or ICER is reported.
What does HTG323 say about budget impact or affordability?
No national budget impact is reported. Use is limited to research and specialist obesity units.
What does HTG323 say about patient quality of life?
Quality of life was among the potential outcomes, but evidence was limited.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in HTG323?
Research-only and specialist-unit requirements constrain delivery to centres with appropriate expertise.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in HTG323?

- Evidence on safety and efficacy is limited in quality and quantity. - Randomised trials had substantial loss to follow-up and risk of bias. - Appropriate clinical indications and durability of weight loss remain uncertain. - Some studies used a prototype rather than the clinically introduced device.
How should the recommendation in HTG323 be implemented in practice?
Use only in research; review local outcomes; record all patients in the National Bariatric Surgery Register; conduct well-controlled studies with detailed safety and technical reporting.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about HTG323?

The device is implanted endoscopically beyond the pylorus and creates an impermeable sleeve approximately 60 cm long that delays mixing of food with digestive enzymes. NICE concluded that the evidence base was insufficient for routine use.
What is NICE guidance HTG423 about?
HTG423 is HealthTech guidance titled "Single-anastomosis duodeno-ileal bypass with sleeve gastrectomy for treating morbid obesity".
When was HTG423 published?
What type of NICE guidance is HTG423?
HealthTech guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in HTG423?

Only use SADI-S with special arrangements for clinical governance, consent and audit or research. Clinicians should inform NHS trust governance leads, explain safety and efficacy uncertainty, review outcomes, use the National Bariatric Surgery Registry, select patients through a multidisciplinary team and use surgeons with specific training in specialist centres.
What condition or clinical problem does HTG423 address?
Morbid obesity, defined as BMI 40 kg/m2 or more, or BMI 35 to under 40 kg/m2 with significant weight-related medical problems.
Who is the target population in HTG423?
People with morbid obesity considered for a metabolic/bariatric surgical procedure, including patients with obesity-related type 2 diabetes.
What intervention is covered by HTG423?
Single-anastomosis duodeno-ileal bypass with sleeve gastrectomy (SADI-S)
What is the current care or treatment standard described in HTG423?
Lifestyle and medical weight management, with bariatric surgery considered for selected patients with severe obesity and comorbidity.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does HTG423 report?

A 100-patient series reported mean excess weight loss of 95% at 12 months, maintained to 48 months; a 97-patient diabetes series reported 92% EWL at 2 years and 98% at 5 years, while a related SIPS series reported 72% EWL at 1 year. Diabetes measures also improved substantially, with reported HbA1c reductions and remission rates of 77% at 2 years and 52% at 5 years in the 97-patient series.
What comparator or comparison does HTG423 use?
Evidence is largely observational and includes related procedures; no robust comparative economic evidence is presented.
What are the main safety considerations in HTG423?

Reported serious events included death from progressive respiratory insufficiency, myocardial infarction, gastric haemorrhage, postoperative gastric leaks (2% in a 100-patient series), duodenal anastomotic leak, haemoperitoneum, abdominal haematoma, trocar-site and umbilical hernias, abscess and sleeve stricture. Hypoalbuminaemia, vitamin A deficiency and raised parathormone were also reported. Specialist advisers identified malnutrition and vitamin/mineral deficiency as theoretical risks.
What does the economic evaluation in HTG423 show?
No formal ICER or health-economic model is reported in the guidance.
What does HTG423 say about budget impact or affordability?
No national cost estimate. Delivery requires specialist centres, trained surgeons, multidisciplinary selection, audit and registry reporting.
What does HTG423 say about patient quality of life?
Quality of life was identified as an efficacy outcome, but the evidence is not presented as a robust comparative QoL dataset.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in HTG423?
Specialist expertise is required; NICE implementation should respect equality duties.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in HTG423?

- Efficacy evidence is limited in quality and quantity. - Potential for serious metabolic complications and revision surgery. - Much of the evidence came from a single centre, limiting generalisability. - Long-term outcomes require further research.
How should the recommendation in HTG423 be implemented in practice?
Use special governance/consent/audit or research arrangements; specialist MDT selection; specifically trained surgeons; local outcomes review; National Bariatric Surgery Registry.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about HTG423?
SADI-S combines sleeve gastrectomy with a duodeno-ileal anastomosis. NICE recognised important potential metabolic complications and possible need for revision procedures.
What is NICE guidance TA494 about?
TA494 is Technology appraisal guidance titled "Naltrexone–bupropion for managing overweight and obesity".
When was TA494 published?
What type of NICE guidance is TA494?
Technology appraisal guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in TA494?

Naltrexone–bupropion is not recommended within its marketing authorisation for managing overweight and obesity in adults alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. This does not affect treatment that was started in the NHS before the guidance was published; existing patients may continue under prior funding arrangements until stopping is considered appropriate.
What condition or clinical problem does TA494 address?
Overweight and obesity in adults; obesity was the main appraisal focus because few trial participants were overweight.
Who is the target population in TA494?
Adults aged 18 years and over with BMI at least 30 kg/m2, or BMI 27 to under 30 kg/m2 with weight-related comorbidity, within the medicine's marketing authorisation.
What intervention is covered by TA494?
Naltrexone–bupropion
Which medicine is assessed in TA494?
Naltrexone–bupropion
What is the brand name mentioned in TA494?
Mysimba
Who is the manufacturer or company associated with TA494?
Orexigen
What is the current care or treatment standard described in TA494?
Lifestyle measures alone or with orlistat, with bariatric surgery for selected patients.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does TA494 report?

Four COR randomised double-blind trials showed greater weight loss with naltrexone–bupropion than placebo: COR-I 6.1% vs 1.3% at week 56; COR-II 6.6% vs 2.1% at week 28; COR-BMOD 9.7% vs 5.5% at week 56 with intensive standard care; and COR-DM 5.1% vs 1.8% at week 56 in type 2 diabetes. Long-term effectiveness remained uncertain.
What comparator or comparison does TA494 use?

The committee considered standard management (lifestyle measures alone) the relevant comparator; orlistat was not representative of usual practice because of gastrointestinal adverse effects and poor adherence.
What are the main safety considerations in TA494?

The appraisal discusses treatment discontinuation, tolerability and uncertainty about long-term treatment. No major safety signal was the central reason for the negative recommendation; the decision was driven mainly by uncertainty in long-term effectiveness, cost effectiveness and potential NHS resource impact.
What does the economic evaluation in TA494 show?

ICER: £23,750 per QALY gained for naltrexone–bupropion plus standard management versus standard management alone. QALYs: Incremental QALY gain about 0.0434; the ICER was sensitive to small changes in QALY estimates. The company's model was a discrete-event simulation. The committee considered the model broadly reasonable after methodological revisions, but uncertainty around weight regain, treatment duration, retreatment and long-term outcomes remained important. Economic modelling and an ICER were reported, but the committee considered the true ICER highly uncertain.
What does TA494 say about budget impact or affordability?
Large numbers of adults could be eligible for potentially long-term treatment, creating potentially high NHS costs; this resource impact contributed to the decision not to recommend.
What does TA494 say about patient quality of life?
Weight and health benefits were incorporated through QALYs; however, the small QALY increment made the ICER very sensitive.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in TA494?
The appraisal considered NHS resource impact and eligibility across a large adult population; no specific access restriction based on ethnicity was central to the decision.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in TA494?

- Long-term effectiveness was unknown. - Weight regain after stopping treatment was uncertain and company assumptions could favour the medicine. - Model could not fully capture retreatment episodes. - Large eligible population and potentially long treatment duration increased decision uncertainty.
What sensitivity or scenario analysis is described in TA494?
ERG and company scenario analyses showed material changes in the ICER with alternative assumptions; the committee concluded there was substantial uncertainty about value for money.
How should the recommendation in TA494 be implemented in practice?
Do not initiate for this indication under the NICE recommendation. Patients already receiving it in the NHS before publication are not required to stop solely because of this guidance.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about TA494?

Mysimba's marketing authorisation covers adults with obesity or overweight with comorbidity. The committee accepted that naltrexone–bupropion might be innovative, but this did not overcome cost-effectiveness uncertainty and potential NHS resource impact.
What is NICE guidance TA664 about?
TA664 is Technology appraisal guidance titled "Liraglutide for managing overweight and obesity".
When was TA664 published?
What type of NICE guidance is TA664?
Technology appraisal guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in TA664?

Liraglutide is recommended as an option for managing overweight and obesity alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity in adults, only for those with BMI at least 35 kg/m2 (or at least 32.5 kg/m2 for specified ethnic groups at equivalent risk), non-diabetic hyperglycaemia, high cardiovascular disease risk, and treatment through a specialist multidisciplinary tier 3 weight-management service, with the commercial arrangement supplied by the company.
What condition or clinical problem does TA664 address?
Adults with overweight/obesity at high cardiovascular risk and non-diabetic hyperglycaemia (prediabetes).
Who is the target population in TA664?
Adults with BMI ≥35 kg/m2 (or ≥32.5 kg/m2 for specified ethnic groups), non-diabetic hyperglycaemia and high cardiovascular disease risk.
What intervention is covered by TA664?
Liraglutide
Which medicine is assessed in TA664?
Liraglutide
What is the brand name mentioned in TA664?
Saxenda
Who is the manufacturer or company associated with TA664?
Novo Nordisk
What is the current care or treatment standard described in TA664?
Lifestyle management, with orlistat or bariatric surgery for selected patients; tier 3 services provide multidisciplinary dietary, behavioural and psychological support.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does TA664 report?

Trial 1839 (3,721 people) included a predefined prediabetes subgroup; the appraisal focused on a post-hoc 800-person subgroup with BMI ≥35, non-diabetic hyperglycaemia and high cardiovascular risk. Liraglutide plus diet/exercise significantly improved weight-related outcomes versus placebo, reduced development of type 2 diabetes and increased reversion to normal glucose tolerance.
What comparator or comparison does TA664 use?
Diet and exercise/lifestyle management alone was the main comparator; orlistat and bariatric surgery were judged not to be realistic alternatives for most people in the target group.
What are the main safety considerations in TA664?

The committee considered the clinical trial evidence to be good quality but recognised uncertainty about longer-term treatment and cardiovascular outcomes. The decision required use within a specialist tier 3 service.
What does the economic evaluation in TA664 show?

ICER: £11,293 per QALY gained in the company's base case; £13,569 per QALY gained in the ERG's preferred base case. Company and ERG base-case ICERs were below the £20,000/QALY threshold; scenario analyses also remained below this level. Formal cost-effectiveness modelling was reported and accepted as cost effective within the specified population/service setting.
What does TA664 say about budget impact or affordability?
Implementation depends on availability of tier 3 specialist weight-management services; the guidance notes variation in access across England.
What does TA664 say about patient quality of life?
Patient experts described obesity as restrictive and stigmatising; multidisciplinary support was considered important for sustaining weight loss.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in TA664?
Lower BMI thresholds apply to specified ethnic minority groups at equivalent cardiometabolic risk; access to tier 3 services varies across England.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in TA664?

- Post-hoc subgroup evidence is more uncertain than the larger predefined prediabetes population. - Long-term cardiovascular benefit was uncertain. - Post-treatment assumptions and calculation of long-term benefits were key modelling uncertainties.
What sensitivity or scenario analysis is described in TA664?
Company and ERG scenario analyses were below £20,000/QALY; committee considered uncertainty when accepting an upper acceptable ICER of £20,000/QALY.
How should the recommendation in TA664 be implemented in practice?
Use only in the specified high-risk adult population through a specialist multidisciplinary tier 3 service, alongside reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about TA664?
Commercial discount details are confidential. The list price in the PDF is £196.20 for 5 x 6 mg/ml 3 ml pre-filled pens, excluding VAT.
What is NICE guidance TA749 about?
TA749 is Technology appraisal guidance titled "Liraglutide for managing obesity in people aged 12 to 17 years (terminated appraisal)".
When was TA749 published?
What type of NICE guidance is TA749?
Technology appraisal guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in TA749?
NICE is unable to make a recommendation about liraglutide for managing obesity in people aged 12 to 17 years.
What condition or clinical problem does TA749 address?
Obesity in young people aged 12 to 17 years.
Who is the target population in TA749?
People aged 12 to 17 years with obesity.
What intervention is covered by TA749?
Liraglutide
Which medicine is assessed in TA749?
Liraglutide
What is the brand name mentioned in TA749?
Saxenda
Who is the manufacturer or company associated with TA749?
Novo Nordisk
What is the current care or treatment standard described in TA749?
No NICE treatment recommendation was made because the appraisal was terminated; NHS organisations were directed to rational local decision making where needed.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does TA749 report?
No full appraisal of clinical effectiveness was conducted because the company did not submit evidence.
What are the main safety considerations in TA749?
Not evaluated in a completed NICE technology appraisal.
What does the economic evaluation in TA749 show?
No economic evaluation was completed because no company evidence submission was provided.
What does TA749 say about budget impact or affordability?
No NICE cost-effectiveness or budget-impact conclusion was made.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in TA749?
NHS organisations considering treatment were advised to follow rational local decision making while no NICE guidance was available.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in TA749?
- No evidence submission was provided for the appraisal. - NICE therefore could not assess clinical or economic effectiveness.
How should the recommendation in TA749 be implemented in practice?
Where NHS organisations wish to consider liraglutide for this indication, use rational local decision-making arrangements in the absence of NICE guidance.
Why was TA749 terminated or unable to make a normal recommendation?

Novo Nordisk did not intend to provide an evidence submission for the appraisal and considered there was not enough evidence to provide one. NICE stated it would review the position if the company decided to make an evidence submission.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about TA749?
This is a very short terminated-appraisal document consisting of advice and information rather than an evidence-based recommendation.
What is NICE guidance HST21 about?
HST21 is Highly specialised technologies guidance titled "Setmelanotide for treating obesity caused by LEPR or POMC deficiency".
When was HST21 published?
What type of NICE guidance is HST21?
Highly specialised technologies guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in HST21?

Setmelanotide is recommended within its marketing authorisation for treating obesity and controlling hunger caused by genetically confirmed biallelic POMC deficiency (including PCSK1 deficiency) or biallelic LEPR deficiency in people aged 6 years and over, provided the company supplies it under the commercial arrangement.
What condition or clinical problem does HST21 address?
Rare genetic disorders of obesity caused by POMC/PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency, associated with early-onset extreme obesity, hyperphagia and substantial quality-of-life burden.
Who is the target population in HST21?
Adults and children aged 6 years and over with genetically confirmed loss-of-function biallelic POMC/PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency and obesity.
What intervention is covered by HST21?
Setmelanotide
Which medicine is assessed in HST21?
Setmelanotide
What is the brand name mentioned in HST21?
Imcivree
Who is the manufacturer or company associated with HST21?
Rhythm Pharmaceuticals
What is the current care or treatment standard described in HST21?
Best supportive care focused on dietary restriction and lifestyle change, including exercise.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does HST21 report?

Evidence came mainly from phase 3 single-arm open-label studies RM-493-012 (POMC deficiency) and RM-493-015 (LEPR deficiency), each enrolling 15 people, with 12 weeks of treatment, blinded withdrawal and 52-week follow-up, plus long-term extension RM-493-022. Results suggested reductions in body weight/BMI and improvements in hunger and quality of life; longer-term benefit appeared sustained but was uncertain.
What comparator or comparison does HST21 use?
Best supportive care was the relevant comparator for the economic evaluation; the index trials were single-arm and used within-model comparisons.
What are the main safety considerations in HST21?
The committee considered adverse events from long-term treatment uncertain but likely tolerable.
What does the economic evaluation in HST21 show?

ICER: £194,630 per QALY gained in the committee's preferred analysis versus best supportive care. The committee judged the most plausible ICER uncertain but likely within the acceptable HST range once QALY weighting and the anticipated higher proportion starting treatment in childhood were considered. A semi-Markov lifetime model was used; multiple assumptions around hyperphagia, utilities, stopping rates and BMI trajectories drove uncertainty.
What does HST21 say about budget impact or affordability?
Specialist-service delivery and the commercial arrangement were required; no public national budget figure is reported in the guidance.
What does HST21 say about patient quality of life?
The committee considered substantial clinical and psychological benefits for people with severe hyperphagia and their carers.
What does HST21 say about caregiver or carer burden?
Carer quality-of-life burden was included in the economic modelling through carer disutility.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in HST21?

Access is limited to genetically confirmed deficiency; people without an identifiable pathogenic variant cannot meet the marketing authorisation. Rare-disease specialist-service access is also required.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in HST21?

- Single-arm index trials limit comparative certainty. - Long-term treatment effect is uncertain. - ICER was sensitive to utility values for severe hyperphagia. - Timing of response assessment and long-term stopping assumptions were uncertain.
What sensitivity or scenario analysis is described in HST21?
Company and ERG scenarios explored different utility, stopping-rate, BMI and treatment-effect assumptions; these materially affected ICERs.
How should the recommendation in HST21 be implemented in practice?
Use within marketing authorisation and commercial arrangement, in specialist highly specialised services with response assessment and ongoing monitoring.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about HST21?
List price £2,376 per 10 mg/ml vial, excluding VAT; confidential NHS discount under a commercial arrangement.
What is NICE guidance TA910 about?
TA910 is Technology appraisal guidance titled "Semaglutide for managing overweight and obesity in young people aged 12 to 17 years (terminated appraisal)".
When was TA910 published?
What type of NICE guidance is TA910?
Technology appraisal guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in TA910?
NICE is unable to make a recommendation about semaglutide for managing overweight and obesity in young people aged 12 to 17 years.
What condition or clinical problem does TA910 address?
Overweight and obesity in young people aged 12 to 17 years.
Who is the target population in TA910?
Young people aged 12 to 17 years with overweight or obesity.
What intervention is covered by TA910?
Semaglutide
Which medicine is assessed in TA910?
Semaglutide
What is the brand name mentioned in TA910?
Wegovy
Who is the manufacturer or company associated with TA910?
Novo Nordisk
What is the current care or treatment standard described in TA910?
No NICE treatment recommendation was made in this terminated appraisal; local decision making applies where treatment is considered.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does TA910 report?
No complete NICE evidence appraisal was performed because no company submission was provided.
What are the main safety considerations in TA910?
Not assessed in a completed technology appraisal.
What does the economic evaluation in TA910 show?
No economic model was submitted or assessed to a completed recommendation standard.
What does TA910 say about budget impact or affordability?
No NICE budget or cost-effectiveness conclusion.
What does TA910 say about patient quality of life?
The company cited inadequate utility evidence to support robust economic modelling.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in TA910?
Local decision making applies while no NICE recommendation is available.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in TA910?
- Insufficient evidence linking adolescent weight loss to long-term clinical outcomes. - Insufficient utility estimates capturing full quality-of-life impact. - No company evidence submission.
How should the recommendation in TA910 be implemented in practice?
Use rational local decision making where NHS organisations consider treatment in the absence of a NICE recommendation.
Why was TA910 terminated or unable to make a normal recommendation?

Novo Nordisk confirmed that it did not intend to make an evidence submission. The company considered there was insufficient evidence to support economic modelling in this population, including insufficient risk equations linking weight loss to long-term outcomes and utility estimates capturing quality-of-life impact.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about TA910?
NICE said it would review the position if the company decided to make an evidence submission.
What is NICE guidance TA875 about?
TA875 is Technology appraisal guidance titled "Semaglutide for managing overweight and obesity".
When was TA875 published?
When was TA875 last updated?
What type of NICE guidance is TA875?
Technology appraisal guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in TA875?

Semaglutide is recommended as an option for weight management, including weight loss and weight maintenance, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity in adults, only if it is used for a maximum of 2 years within a specialist multidisciplinary weight-management service, the person has at least one weight-related comorbidity, and the company provides it under the commercial arrangement. BMI thresholds are usually reduced by 2.5 kg/m2 for specified ethnic groups. Consider stopping if less than 5% of initial weight has been lost after 6 months.
What condition or clinical problem does TA875 address?
Adult overweight and obesity requiring specialist management, with associated cardiometabolic morbidity.
Who is the target population in TA875?

Adults with BMI ≥35 kg/m2 plus at least one weight-related comorbidity, or BMI 30.0 to 34.9 kg/m2 meeting specialist referral criteria, within specialist weight-management services; lower BMI thresholds apply for specified ethnic groups.
What intervention is covered by TA875?
Semaglutide
Which medicine is assessed in TA875?
Semaglutide
What is the brand name mentioned in TA875?
Wegovy
Who is the manufacturer or company associated with TA875?
Novo Nordisk
What is the current care or treatment standard described in TA875?
Lifestyle measures alone or with orlistat, and specialist weight-management services that may include liraglutide or bariatric surgery.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does TA875 report?

STEP 1 was a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial. The committee concluded that semaglutide produced substantially greater weight loss with supervised weight-management support than support alone, and more weight loss than liraglutide. Cardiovascular and metabolic benefits were also considered.
What comparator or comparison does TA875 use?
Diet and exercise/weight-management support was the main comparator; liraglutide was used as a comparator for a high-risk subgroup with non-diabetic hyperglycaemia and high cardiovascular risk.
What are the main safety considerations in TA875?
The appraisal considered treatment duration, weight regain after stopping, and longer-term evidence. The recommendation limits treatment to a maximum of 2 years in the specialist service setting.
What does the economic evaluation in TA875 show?

ICER: £14,827 per QALY gained in the company's base case and £16,337 per QALY gained in the ERG base case for the original target population versus diet/exercise support. Scenario analyses generally remained below £20,000/QALY, although lower starting BMI, longer treatment duration and inclusion of some broader populations increased the ICER. Cohort-transition model with 11 health states and a maximum of 3 years modelled treatment in the original economic analysis.
What does TA875 say about budget impact or affordability?

NICE noted that expanding treatment to a much larger lower-BMI population would have important NHS service-delivery implications; specialist multidisciplinary capacity was therefore part of the recommendation.
What does TA875 say about patient quality of life?
Weight-management benefit and long-term health outcomes were captured through QALYs.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in TA875?
Lower BMI thresholds are advised for specified ethnic groups; access to specialist weight-management services varies and the committee considered service-delivery implications.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in TA875?

- Long-term effectiveness and treatment duration are uncertain. - Weight regain after stopping treatment is uncertain. - Trial/model population distribution may not fully represent the general eligible population, especially at lower BMI. - Cardiovascular benefit assumptions were uncertain but did not overturn cost effectiveness.
What sensitivity or scenario analysis is described in TA875?

ERG scenarios showed ICER increases to £22,192/QALY at a lower mean starting BMI and £21,060/QALY with alternative weight-advantage assumptions; company/ERG scenarios supported the need for a restricted population and duration.
How should the recommendation in TA875 be implemented in practice?
Prescribe through specialist multidisciplinary weight-management services; combine with diet and physical activity; apply BMI thresholds and stopping criteria in the recommendation.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about TA875?
List prices in the PDF: £175.80 per 2.4 mg pack, £124.53 per 1.7 mg pack, and £73.25 per pack for 0.25/0.5/1.0 mg strengths, excluding VAT; commercial discount is confidential.
What is NICE guidance HTG711 about?
HTG711 is HealthTech guidance titled "Endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty for obesity".
When was HTG711 published?
What type of NICE guidance is HTG711?
HealthTech guidance.

Use endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty as an option to treat obesity in adults with standard arrangements for clinical governance, consent and audit. Obesity, defined as BMI 30 kg/m2 or over; class 1 30-34.9, class 2 35-39.9 and class 3 40 or more.

Adults with obesity, including people for whom non-surgical treatment has not worked and people with class 3 obesity for whom invasive bariatric surgery would be considered high risk.

Endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty
What is the current care or treatment standard described in HTG711?
Lifestyle management, medicines and bariatric surgery for selected patients; ESG offers a less invasive endoscopic option.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does HTG711 report?

The committee concluded that evidence showed people with BMI over 30 kg/m2 can lose weight when ESG is combined with lifestyle change. Key outcomes for ongoing data collection include total and excess weight loss, quality of life, comorbidity improvement, nutritional status and technical success.
What comparator or comparison does HTG711 use?
No formal economic comparator analysis; clinical evidence supports effectiveness with lifestyle change.
What are the main safety considerations in HTG711?

The committee considered evidence on short- and long-term safety adequate for standard arrangements but noted self-limiting early side effects and a high incidence of readmission for abdominal pain when performed as a day case. What does the economic evaluation in HTG711 show?
No formal ICER is reported.
What does HTG711 say about budget impact or affordability?

What does HTG711 say about patient quality of life?
Quality of life is a key outcome for ongoing follow-up.

Use only in specialist weight-management centres with MDT assessment/monitoring, trained clinicians, governance/consent/audit and National Bariatric Surgery Registry submission.

NICE considered the procedure safe in the short and long term and sufficiently supported by efficacy evidence for standard arrangements.
What is NICE guidance HST31 about?

When was HST31 published?
What type of NICE guidance is HST31?
Highly specialised technologies guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in HST31?

Setmelanotide is recommended as an option for treating obesity and hyperphagia in genetically confirmed Bardet-Biedl syndrome in people aged 6 years and over, only if they are aged 6 to 17 when treatment starts. What condition or clinical problem does HST31 address?
Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS), a rare genetic disorder associated with hyperphagia, severe early-onset obesity and multiple systemic manifestations.
Who is the target population in HST31?
People with genetically confirmed BBS aged 6 years and over, but routine commissioning is restricted to those who start treatment between ages 6 and 17.
What intervention is covered by HST31?
Setmelanotide
Which medicine is assessed in HST31?
Setmelanotide
What is the brand name mentioned in HST31?
Imcivree
Who is the manufacturer or company associated with HST31?
Rhythm Pharmaceuticals
What is the current care or treatment standard described in HST31?
Best supportive care with dietary restriction, lifestyle measures and multidisciplinary management; there was no disease-targeting pharmacological option before setmelanotide.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does HST31 report?

The pivotal RM-493-023 phase 3 study enrolled 44 people and had a 14-week randomised placebo-controlled phase followed by open-label treatment. At week 52, mean weight reduction in the BBS pivotal cohort was 9.4 kg (8%); 46.7% of adults achieved at least 10% weight loss versus a 10% historical CRIBBS registry rate, and 85.7% of children/young people achieved a BMI-Z reduction of at least 0.2. Hunger and quality of life also improved.
What comparator or comparison does HST31 use?
Best supportive care was the relevant comparator. Bariatric surgery and semaglutide were not considered appropriate primary comparators for BBS.
What are the main safety considerations in HST31?
The committee considered long-term adverse-event evidence and uncertainties in treatment effect; the overall safety profile was considered manageable in the specialist setting.
What does the economic evaluation in HST31 show?

ICER: £174,904 per QALY gained for the committee's preferred mixed adult/child population; £171,844 per QALY gained when everyone entered the model as children. With QALY weighting, the mixed population remained above the acceptable threshold, whereas the childhood-start subgroup was within the threshold. The committee used a lifetime model with 7 BMI-Z classes for children, 7 BMI classes for adults and death, with treatment response assessed around 14 weeks. Economic conclusions were highly sensitive to starting age, hyperphagia distribution, treatment-effect assumptions, utilities and stopping rates.
What does HST31 say about budget impact or affordability?
Confidential commercial discount. Routine commissioning was restricted to childhood initiation because the mixed population was not sufficiently cost effective despite QALY weighting.
What does HST31 say about patient quality of life?
The committee recognised substantial impact of hyperphagia and BBS on people and families and considered setmelanotide potentially innovative.
What does HST31 say about caregiver or carer burden?
Carer quality-of-life burden was explicitly considered, including possible benefits beyond direct patient health gain.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in HST31?

The recommendation excludes people who start treatment in adulthood; around 20% may lack an identifiable genetic variant and therefore cannot meet genetically confirmed access criteria. Ethnic inequalities were considered.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in HST31?

- Long-term evidence and durability of treatment benefit remain uncertain. - Week-52 open-label outcomes are vulnerable to regression-to-the-mean/placebo effects. - Economic modelling depended on uncertain hyperphagia prevalence/severity, utilities, BMI transitions and stopping rates. - Managed access for adult starters could not be recommended because no proposal was submitted.
What sensitivity or scenario analysis is described in HST31?
Company, EAG and committee scenarios included alternative hyperphagia distributions, BMI-Z class shifts, placebo-effect adjustments, stopping rates and utility values; these materially changed ICERs.
How should the recommendation in HST31 be implemented in practice?
Initiate in the recommended age window under specialist care, assess response in multidisciplinary practice, continue only under the commercial arrangement, and follow implementation requirements.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about HST31?

The PDF lists a list price of £2,376.00 per 10 mg/ml vial, excluding VAT, with a confidential commercial arrangement. The recommendation specifically distinguishes children who start treatment at age 6-17 from people starting in adulthood.

Quality standard.

Overweight, obesity and central adiposity as chronic, relapsing and progressive conditions associated with increased morbidity and mortality.

What is NICE guidance TA1026 about?

When was TA1026 published?
When was TA1026 last updated?
What type of NICE guidance is TA1026?
Technology appraisal guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in TA1026?

Tirzepatide is recommended as an option for managing overweight and obesity alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity in adults only if initial BMI is at least 35 kg/m2, there is at least one weight-related comorbidity, and the company provides tirzepatide under the commercial arrangement. Lower BMI thresholds usually reduced by 2.5 kg/m2 apply for specified ethnic groups. If less than 5% of initial weight is lost after 6 months on the highest tolerated dose, continuation should be reconsidered.
What condition or clinical problem does TA1026 address?
Adult overweight and obesity with important cardiometabolic and other weight-related comorbidities.
Who is the target population in TA1026?
Adults with initial BMI ≥35 kg/m2 and at least one weight-related comorbidity; lower BMI threshold usually 2.5 kg/m2 lower for specified ethnic groups.
What intervention is covered by TA1026?
Tirzepatide
Which medicine is assessed in TA1026?
Tirzepatide
What is the brand name mentioned in TA1026?
Mounjaro
Who is the manufacturer or company associated with TA1026?
Eli Lilly
What is the current care or treatment standard described in TA1026?
Diet and exercise support, specialist overweight/obesity management and existing pharmacological options such as semaglutide; bariatric surgery for selected patients.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does TA1026 report?

SURMOUNT-1 was a randomised double-blind trial comparing tirzepatide with placebo, both alongside diet and exercise support, in adults with obesity or overweight with qualifying comorbidity. The appraisal found substantial weight-management benefit but noted that people with type 2 diabetes and some severe psychiatric disorders were not represented, limiting generalisability to the full licensed population.
What comparator or comparison does TA1026 use?
The economic appraisal compared tirzepatide with diet/exercise support and with semaglutide.
What are the main safety considerations in TA1026?

The committee reviewed adverse events and population exclusions and noted uncertainties for people with type 2 diabetes and severe psychiatric disorders. Treatment is accompanied by monitoring and a response reassessment at 6 months.
What does the economic evaluation in TA1026 show?

An individual patient simulation model used 4-week cycles for the first 2 years and annual cycles thereafter. Risk equations translated surrogate outcomes such as BMI into long-term events, which introduced uncertainty. Committee-preferred analyses suggested ICERs for the broadly licensed population above the acceptable level, while the subgroup with BMI ≥35 kg/m2 and at least one comorbidity was around or below the acceptable ICER. Full ICER figures varied by scenario; the guidance focused on the restricted BMI/comorbidity subgroup as sufficiently close to cost-effective.
What does TA1026 say about budget impact or affordability?

Budget impact: NICE estimated around 3.4 million adults could be eligible under the marketing authorisation, with at least 220,000 expected to receive NHS-funded treatment within the first 3 years under the interim commissioning/prioritisation arrangements. Introduction is phased through NHS England commissioning arrangements. Service capacity and delivery models are major implementation considerations.
What does TA1026 say about patient quality of life?
Weight loss and downstream health benefits drive QALY gains; access to obesity services was recognised as unequal across England.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in TA1026?

Lower BMI thresholds for specified ethnic groups; implementation considered geographic inequality in access to specialist services and the need to accommodate people with learning disabilities and severe mental illness.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in TA1026?

- SURMOUNT-1 did not include people with type 2 diabetes, so the full licensed population is not directly represented. - Long-term outcomes rely on risk equations and extrapolation rather than direct trial evidence. - Service delivery costs and models were uncertain. - Weight regain after stopping treatment and transferability from other GLP-1 treatments were debated.
What sensitivity or scenario analysis is described in TA1026?

Multiple scenarios changed treatment effect, stopping/weight regain and service-delivery assumptions; broader target populations produced higher ICERs and were not accepted for routine recommendation.
How should the recommendation in TA1026 be implemented in practice?
Use with diet and physical activity, apply BMI/comorbidity eligibility and 6-month response review, and follow NHS England's phased commissioning and service-delivery arrangements.
What important context should an LLM know when answering questions about TA1026?

What is NICE guidance TA1152 about?

When was TA1152 published?
What type of NICE guidance is TA1152?
Technology appraisal guidance.
What is NICE's recommendation in TA1152?

Semaglutide, up to a maintenance dose of 2.4 mg once weekly, can be used within its marketing authorisation alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2).
What condition or clinical problem does TA1152 address?
Adults with established cardiovascular disease (previous myocardial infarction, stroke or peripheral arterial disease) and overweight or obesity.
Who is the target population in TA1152?
Adults with established CVD and BMI ≥27 kg/m2 within the semaglutide cardiovascular-risk-reduction indication.
What intervention is covered by TA1152?
Semaglutide
Which medicine is assessed in TA1152?
Semaglutide
What is the brand name mentioned in TA1152?
Wegovy
Who is the manufacturer or company associated with TA1152?
Novo Nordisk
What is the current care or treatment standard described in TA1152?
Standard cardiovascular secondary prevention and healthy-lifestyle advice, with medicines to lower cardiovascular risk.
What clinical effectiveness or efficacy evidence does TA1152 report?

SELECT was the key multinational randomised double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 trial. Semaglutide plus standard care reduced the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events versus placebo plus standard care. Benefit appeared soon after starting treatment, before substantial weight loss, suggesting an effect independent of weight loss. STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM provided supportive evidence.
What comparator or comparison does TA1152 use?
Placebo plus standard care was the main trial comparator; the economic model represented standard care in addition to semaglutide.

ICER: £6,878 to £14,594 per QALY gained depending on the cardiovascular-event-rate adjustment approach; preferred ICERs were substantially below £20,000/QALY. A state-transition model included recurrent cardiovascular events, chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes and death. The lead team judged the cost-effectiveness estimates robust enough to accept despite uncertainty about time on treatment and healthy-lifestyle counselling costs. Cost-effectiveness estimates remained comfortably within the NICE threshold across plausible approaches.
What does TA1152 say about budget impact or affordability?
No national budget-impact figure is presented in the appraisal excerpt; affordability was judged acceptable given the low ICERs.
What does TA1152 say about patient quality of life?
Benefits from preventing cardiovascular events are captured through QALYs.
What equality, equity or access issues are addressed in TA1152?

Implementation should accommodate people with language difficulties or cognitive impairment; the lead team emphasised accessible lifestyle interventions and did not treat these issues as reasons to deny treatment.
What are the main evidence gaps or uncertainties in TA1152?

- Uncertainty remained about duration of semaglutide treatment. - The modelled cost of additional healthy-lifestyle counselling was uncertain. - Some cardiovascular-event differences in SELECT were not statistically significant but were retained in the preferred modelling approach.
What sensitivity or scenario analysis is described in TA1152?
The lead team tested alternative cardiovascular-event-rate adjustments and treatment-cost assumptions; preferred ICERs remained below £20,000/QALY.
How should the recommendation in TA1152 be implemented in practice?
Use semaglutide within the cardiovascular-risk-reduction marketing authorisation at up to 2.4 mg weekly, alongside standard cardiovascular care, reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.

NICE guideline.

Overweight and obesity management

What is NICE guidance NG202 about?

When was NG202 published?
What type of NICE guidance is NG202?
NICE guideline.

OSAHS, OHS and COPD-OSAHS overlap syndrome in adults over 16; obesity is an important risk factor and contributor to severity, particularly for OHS.

Adults over 16 with suspected or diagnosed OSAHS, OHS or COPD-OSAHS overlap syndrome.

OSAHS/OHS management

Sleep-history assessment, diagnostic testing, tailored lifestyle advice and positive-airway-pressure therapy, with specialist sleep-service follow-up.

Diagnostic strategies include home respiratory polygraphy, home oximetry and hospital-based testing; treatment comparisons include CPAP versus non-invasive ventilation in appropriate OHS populations.

The committee judged the treatment effect larger in children and found the mixed adult/child population insufficiently cost effective, whereas the model for people starting as children fell within the acceptable range after QALY weighting.
What was the committee’s preferred ICER for HST31?

The preferred ICER was about £174,904 per QALY gained in the mixed adult/child population and £171,844 per QALY gained when everyone entered the model as children. QALY weighting allowed the childhood-start subgroup to meet the acceptable threshold but not the mixed population.
Is QS212 a treatment recommendation?
No. QS212 is a quality standard. It defines eight measurable quality statements for overweight and obesity management rather than recommending or rejecting a treatment.
What are the eight quality statements in QS212?

They cover annual BMI and waist-to-height measurement in adults with long-term conditions; BMI recording in children and young people over 2; supported access for people with a learning disability; maintaining service information; providing information about interventions and services; wraparound care with weight-management medicines; support after stopping medicines or completing behavioural interventions; and annual shared-care follow-up after bariatric surgery.
What is the main equity focus of QS212?

Improving equitable access and delivery, including support for people with learning disabilities, ethnicity-adjusted BMI thresholds, reasonable adjustments for disability, accessible information, and attention to health inequalities.
Who is eligible for tirzepatide under TA1026?

Adults with a BMI of at least 35 kg/m2 and at least one weight-related comorbidity, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity, subject to the commercial arrangement. Lower BMI thresholds apply for specified ethnic groups at equivalent risk.
What happens if weight loss is insufficient with tirzepatide in TA1026?
Treatment continuation is subject to a 6-month response review; the guidance uses a threshold based on achieving at least 5% loss of initial body weight on the highest tolerated dose.
What was the scale of the potential NHS population for tirzepatide?

NICE estimated about 3.4 million adults could be eligible under the marketing authorisation, with at least 220,000 expected to receive NHS-funded treatment within the first 3 years under the interim commissioning and prioritisation arrangements described in the guidance.
What is semaglutide used for in TA1152?

Semaglutide, up to a maintenance dose of 2.4 mg once weekly, can be used alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and BMI at least 27 kg/m2.
What was the main clinical evidence for TA1152?

The SELECT randomised double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 trial showed that semaglutide plus standard care reduced major adverse cardiovascular events compared with placebo plus standard care. Benefit appeared before substantial weight loss, suggesting an effect not explained solely by weight loss.
Was semaglutide cost effective in TA1152?
Yes. Reported ICERs ranged from about £6,878 to £14,594 per QALY gained depending on the cardiovascular-event-rate adjustment approach, remaining below £20,000 per QALY.
What does NG246 cover?

It provides comprehensive recommendations on preventing, identifying and assessing overweight, obesity and central adiposity, behavioural interventions, diet, physical activity, medicines, surgery, digital delivery, service planning and monitoring across ages.
What equity considerations are included in NG246?

The guideline includes lower BMI thresholds for specified ethnic groups, reasonable adjustments for people with disabilities, accessible information, and attention to health inequalities and person-centred care.
When should bariatric surgery be considered in NG246?

The guideline recommends referral for bariatric surgery assessment at BMI 40 kg/m2 or more, or BMI 35 to 39.9 kg/m2 with a significant health condition that could improve with weight loss, subject to the detailed eligibility and pathway recommendations.
What conditions are covered by NG202?
Obstructive sleep apnoea/hypopnoea syndrome (OSAHS), obesity hypoventilation syndrome (OHS), and COPD–OSAHS overlap syndrome in people over 16.
How is OSAHS generally assessed under NG202?
The guideline recommends structured clinical assessment followed by appropriate diagnostic testing, including home or hospital-based testing according to the person and the sleep-service pathway.
What treatment approach is recommended for OHS with severe OSAHS and no acute ventilatory failure?
CPAP is generally preferred first line because it is simpler and more cost effective, with non-invasive ventilation used when appropriate or when CPAP is not suitable or effective.
